Question: What is an example of 'mansplaining'?
Answer: This happened here on Quora. I wrote an answer about how a guy rejected my elder sister's marriage proposal because she has spectacles and his parents didn't want their future children to have spectacles too. I put in a sentence about how my dad, who is an ophthalmologist, explained how myopia (short sightedness) has a lot of other causes apart from heredity. This one guy in the comments section said my claims are 'bullsh*t', and added a link to a random Google article. I am a doctor. My father is an opthalmologist. And yet this guy, who was an engineer, explained to me how eyesight works and how I was wrong because, duhh..Google! I was supposed to trust a random link shared by a stranger from Quora over the tons of books that me and my dad have read over the years. I mean, me and my dad like have legitimate degrees and all! That my friend, is mansplaining.

Name: Siya Patil
Question: How has the coronavirus affected you?
Answer: Corona…6 lettered word that has stopped the world. When it was spreading all over but not in India, I wasn't really worried. Or I chose to not worry.. ignorance is bliss right? But as it spread in US, panic started to set in. My sister and her family, my brother and my husband all live in US. And now it's spreading in India, where I live with my parents and in laws and all of my extended family. My cousin lives in Italy and is in quarantine. So basically,now it is a constant source of worry. I am worried about my brother, who's a little reckless and his City is one of the worst affected. Though he is working from home, his roommate still has to go to work. I keep warning him about taking precautions and I just hope he is telling the truth when he says he's being careful, my sister is working from home and my niece and nephew have started home schooling. My husband's working from home and I know he's being very cautious. I am upset that I won't be meeting him in June, because I am pretty sure this isn't gonna be ok till then. My parents are in their 60s. My mother is diabetic. My father is an ophthalmologist and still goes to his clinic everyday. And I really worried about them. I am trying not to visit them much since I am a doctor and I worried I might catch it. My niece in India is at home since her school and dance classes have closed down. As for me..I am still coming to work everyday. We have cancelled most elective surgeries but are still going forward with the emergency ones. I see most patients coming with masks. We have 1 positive patient in our city. Though none in my hospital. I am a surgeon, hence I am not yet in direct service for corona patients or suspects. But I am prepared that if situation worsens all the man power will be shifted to caring for those affected with COVID 19 and I will be ready and willing when that happens. As of now, I'm seeing my surgical patients, doing emergency duties and washing my hands like a maniac! This is me, before my emergency shift. This is all the PPE we get, because of the acute shortage of PPE everywhere. Take care everyone, it's not as simple as it seems right now. Stay home, stay safe just because you can. I wish I could too, but I cannot. STAY AWAY FROM CROWDED PLACES. DO NOT GO OUT IN GROUPS. AND WASH YOUR HANDS. AS MANY TIMES AS YOU THINK IS NECESSARY, PLUS ONE. Constant vigilance!

Name: Siya Patil
Question: How has your life improved recently?
Answer: I started my residency in general surgery 2 months back! So, after completing my MBBS, I struggled for a few years trying to crack my post graduate entrance. I was getting other specialities, just not the one I wanted. So I waited, and tried. Over and over again. It was an all consuming fire. I lost so much in it. Time, effort, relationship, sanity. I went into clinical depression near the end. Just when I was about to give up…the clouds parted, sunshine seeped through! I got a good rank, I got into the residency of my choice .. general surgery! My dream finally came true. Is it hectic? Hell yeah. I work all day. Don't get enough sleep most nights, meals are never on time. But every single morning that I go to work, I can't help but feel grateful. I appreciate every single suture and incision that I give. You know why? Because I have seen what life is without that. This is how my life has improved recently. I went from being a doctor to being a surgeon. And I wouldn't trade it for the world.

Question: Have you ever seen a doctor yell at their patient?
Answer: I was that doctor. I yelled, loudly, not at the patient but at her aunt. So I was working in the ER. A little kid of around 10 or 11 came late one evening. She had a massive blow on her skull and was getting seizures. It was all bloody but surprisingly she was conscious. Her aunt was very caring and hovering over us. She told me the girl fell from a bike. I pacified her and told her to wait outside while I provided primary care to the child before transferring her to a higher care centre. When the aunt was outside I asked the girl what happened. Her aunt had hit her in the head with a hammer. That vile lady had hit her 10-year-old niece in the head with a hammer. I was horrified, enraged. I was mad. I stabilized her, came out and called the aunt inside. As soon as I saw her I just lost it. I yelled at her at the top of my lungs. I don't even remember all that I said but it lasted long enough for the ward boys and nurses and the ambulance driver to gather. It also lasted enough for the aunt to break down and confess. I called the girl’s parents and they called the police and registered the complaint. My behaviour was unprofessional, but I have never regretted it. I don't usually lose my cool, but I am glad I did that day.
